## Setup and Package Loading
```{r setup, message=FALSE}

setwd("/Users/bishtananya/Desktop/Bioinformatics")
library(tximport)
library(DESeq2)
library(tidyverse)
library(pheatmap)
library(EnhancedVolcano)
```

```{r}
# 
library(biomaRt)

# 1. Connect to the human Ensembl database (GRCh38 build)
mart <- useMart("ensembl", dataset = "hsapiens_gene_ensembl")

# 2. Download the transcript IDs and their matching gene symbols
tx2gene <- getBM(
    attributes = c("ensembl_transcript_id_version", "external_gene_name"),
    mart = mart
)

# 3. Rename columns so tximport recognizes them automatically
colnames(tx2gene) <- c("tx_id", "gene_id")

# 4. Take a quick peek at your new mapping table
head(tx2gene)


# 5. Clean the transcript IDs by removing the "." and any numbers after it
tx2gene$tx_id <- gsub("\\..*$", "", tx2gene$tx_id)

```


```{r}
# importing kallisto data into R

# Use the absolute path to your folder
base_dir <- "/Users/bishtananya/Desktop/Bioinformatics"

samples <- c("SRR28816867", "SRR28816868","SRR28816869", "SRR28816870", "SRR28816871", "SRR28816872", "SRR28816873", "SRR28816874") 

# Construct the paths explicitly
files <- file.path(base_dir, paste0("result_", samples), "abundance.tsv")
names(files) <- samples


# 2. Look at your table again to make sure the decimals are gone
head(tx2gene)

# Run the translator
txi <- tximport(
    files = files, 
    type = "kallisto", 
    tx2gene = tx2gene, 
    ignoreTxVersion = TRUE
)

```



```{r}
# 1. Create a matching data frame for your 8 samples
# WARNING: Make sure the order of "Control" and "Treated" perfectly matches the order of your 'samples' vector!
sampleTable <- data.frame(
    sampleName = samples,
    condition = factor(c("Treated", "Control", "Treated", "Control", 
                         "Treated", "Control", "Treated", "Control"))
)

# 2. Set the row names to match your sample IDs
rownames(sampleTable) <- sampleTable$sampleName

# 3. Double-check your metadata table
sampleTable

library(DESeq2)

```

```{r}
library(DESeq2)

# 1. Build the dataset object
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromTximport(txi, colData = sampleTable, design = ~ condition)

# 2. RUN ONLY THE MATH (We use parallel = FALSE to prevent Mac memory freezes)
dds <- DESeq(dds, parallel = FALSE)

# 3. Pull the raw results immediately
res <- results(dds, contrast = c("condition", "Treated", "Control"))

# 4. View it as a raw table first (avoids tidyverse conflicts for now)
head(res)

```
```{r}
summary(res)
```
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Turn the raw results into a clean, queryable data frame
res_df <- as.data.frame(res) %>%
    rownames_to_column(var = "gene_name") %>%
    as_tibble()

# 2. Permanently filter out the structural background noise using regex
biologically_clean_df <- res_df %>% 
    filter(!str_detect(gene_name, "rRNA|RNA5-|^7SK|^U\\d+|^H[1-4][A-Z]|^H\\d|MT-|^LINC|^SNORD|^MIR|^RNU|^RNY"))

biologically_clean_df <- biologically_clean_df %>%
    filter(log2FoldChange != "NA") %>%
    filter(padj != "NA")

# 3. run your statistical thresholds using the newly polished data
sig_up <- biologically_clean_df %>% 
    filter(padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange > 1) %>% 
    arrange(padj)

sig_down <- biologically_clean_df %>% 
    filter(padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange < -1) %>% 
    arrange(padj)

# 4. Save CSV files 
write_csv(sig_up, "DESeq2_significant_UP_genes.csv")
write_csv(sig_down, "DESeq2_significant_DOWN_genes.csv")


# 4. See how many genes made the cut
nrow(sig_up)

nrow(sig_down)

```


```{r}
EnhancedVolcano(biologically_clean_df,
    lab = biologically_clean_df$gene_name,
    x = 'log2FoldChange',
    y = 'padj',
    pCutoff = 0.05,
    FCcutoff = 1.0,
    pointSize = 2.0,
    labSize = 4.0,
    title = 'Treated vs Control Differential Expression',
    subtitle = 'Pristine Protein-Coding mRNAs Only',
    legendPosition = 'right')
```

```{r}

library(DESeq2)
library(pheatmap)
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Transform the raw counts data to stabilize the variance
vsd <- vst(dds, blind = FALSE)

# 2. Get the gene names of your top 50 most statistically significant hits
# (We combine top 25 UP and top 25 DOWN for a beautifully balanced look)
top_up_genes <- sig_up %>% head(25) %>% pull(gene_name)
top_down_genes <- sig_down %>% head(25) %>% pull(gene_name)
top_genes <- c(top_up_genes, top_down_genes)

# 3. Extract the normalized expression matrix for just these 50 genes
mat <- assay(vsd)[top_genes, ]

# 4. Change row names from Ensembl IDs to your clean gene symbols
# (Assuming your vsd matrix row names match your original dataframe order)
rownames(mat) <- top_genes

# 5. Create a clean metadata dataframe to color-code the top of your columns
df_annotation <- as.data.frame(colData(dds)["condition"])

# 6. Draw the beautiful heatmap!
pheatmap(mat, 
         annotation_col = df_annotation, 
         scale = "row",                # Scales genes so we see RELATIVE changes
         clustering_distance_rows = "correlation",
         clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean",
         show_rownames = TRUE, 
         show_colnames = FALSE,         # Hides messy raw sample names
         fontsize_row = 7,
         cellheight = 10,
         main = "Top 50 Differentially Expressed Genes")


```

```{r}
library(gprofiler2)
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Extract just the gene names from your upregulated list
upregulated_genes <- sig_up %>% pull(gene_name)

# 2. Run the enrichment profile against Human database (hsapiens)
go_results <- gost(query = upregulated_genes, 
                   organism = "hsapiens", 
                   ordered_query = TRUE, # Prioritizes your most significant genes
                   sources = c("GO:BP", "KEGG")) # Focuses on Biological Processes and KEGG pathways

# 3. Plot the interactive results chart
gostplot(go_results, capped = TRUE, interactive = TRUE)
```

```{r}


# Convert the results into a readable dataframe and look at the top rows
go_table <- as.data.frame(go_results$result) %>%
  dplyr::select(source, term_id, term_name, p_value, intersection_size) %>%
  arrange(p_value)

# Print the top 10 results to your console
head(go_table, 10)

# Save the pathway results to your project folder
write_csv(go_table, "GO_and_KEGG_Enrichment_Results.csv")

```

```{r}

# Filter for the top 10 biological processes and plot them
top_10_go <- go_table %>% 
  filter(source == "GO:BP") %>% 
  head(10)

ggplot(top_10_go, aes(x = reorder(term_name, -log10(p_value)), y = -log10(p_value))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Biological Process", y = "-log10(p-value)", 
       title = "Top 10 Enriched Biological Processes") +
  theme_minimal()

```
